interface.title: GeneScape (v1.0.6)
interface.stage_of_work: Interpreting results: functional characterization of a gene list after an experiment such as differential expression
interface.what_it_is_for: Turn a pasted list of genes or GO ids into a drawn Gene Ontology subgraph and a coverage table of the functions they share, narrowed by coverage, word filter and GO domain, for one of nine organisms.

data.note: I used the human gene list the textarea is prefilled with (12 genes such as CEACAM20 and NEUROD2) and the organism annotation indexes bundled with the tool (goa_human, mgi, sgd and the Arabidopsis index). The app has no upload control, so the test files could not be loaded. Instead I typed equivalent lists: a gene, a GO id and the invalid symbol FOO; 8 mouse genes; 8 yeast cell-cycle genes; 4 GO ids; and TP53/BRCA1 for Arabidopsis.

features.name: Ontology subgraph viewer with coverage-coloured nodes
features.general: Draw the part of a hierarchy reached from a set of items. Colour nodes by branch and highlight the terms the items actually carry, with how common each term is overall and how many items carry it, so general and specific terms can be told apart. Then zoom around the drawing.
features.specific: Draw Tree renders the GO DAG client-side (viz-js). Nodes are beige for BP, blue for MF and pink for CC. Terms the input genes carry are green, and dark green for terms that are leaves of the ontology (most specific possible), whether or not they sit at the bottom of the drawn subgraph. Each node shows [total annotations across the organism's genes] and (k/N input genes). Zoom in, Zoom out and Reset rescale the drawing.
steps: Press Draw Tree
Read the branch colours and green annotated nodes
Compare [N] with (k/N) and note dark-green ontology leaves to judge specificity
Zoom out to see the whole graph or zoom in to read labels
Reset to native scale
serves_tasks: Generate the hierarchy graph for the list
Judge how specific each shared function is

features.name: Coverage threshold with automatic estimate
features.general: Set a minimum count of items that must share a category before it is shown. If no value is given, the tool picks a sensible cutoff and reports it.
features.specific: Leave Coverage blank and Annotations reports 'Automatically estimated coverage cutoff: 5'. Typing 3 or 1 and pressing Draw Tree grows the tree (18 to 68 nodes), and a higher value shrinks it. The summary line echoes 'Coverage set to N' with the node and edge counts.
steps: Leave Coverage blank and draw to get the automatic cutoff
Read the cutoff and graph size on the Annotations tab
Type a lower or higher Coverage
Press Draw Tree again and compare node counts
serves_tasks: Set how many items must share a function
Generate the hierarchy graph for the list

features.name: Theme and branch filters with empty-result message
features.general: Keep only categories in one branch of the hierarchy and/or whose names match a pattern, so the hierarchy shows one theme. These filters apply together with the minimum count, and the tool says clearly when nothing passes.
features.specific: Domain (Biological Process, Cellular Component or Molecular Function) keeps one GO branch. Word filter (regex ok) keeps GO terms whose Function matches, for example 'transcription|DNA' or 'kinase'. Both work together with Coverage. When nothing passes, the app shows 'No GO terms pass all filtering conditions' with the conditions it used.
steps: Choose a Domain, or leave all three branches
Type a word or regex in Word filter
Optionally combine with a Coverage value
Press Draw Tree
Check the trimmed graph and table, or the no-match message
serves_tasks: Keep only functions matching a theme
Restrict to one branch of the hierarchy

features.name: Identifier list input with unknown-symbol report
features.general: Paste a list of identifiers of mixed types, one per line, check them against a chosen reference database, and list any that are not recognised above the result.
features.specific: The Gene List textarea accepts gene symbols, UniProt accessions and GO ids, one per line; a space-separated line is read as one unknown symbol. The Organism dropdown picks the GAF index (human, mouse, rat, fly, zebrafish, worm, E. coli, yeast, Arabidopsis). Unmatched entries are listed in red as 'N unkown symbols: ...'.
steps: Paste identifiers into Gene List, one per line
Choose Organism
Press Draw Tree
Read the red unknown-symbols list and fix the input
serves_tasks: Enter a list of item identifiers, one per line, mixed types allowed
Choose the reference database for the species
Check which input identifiers were not recognised

features.name: Filterable, sortable result table
features.general: Show the same result as a table with a filter box under each column and a numeric min/max range, and sort by clicking column headers.
features.specific: The Annotations tab shows Coverage, Function, Domain (BP/MF/CC), GO and Genes (pipe-separated). It has a min/max filter on Coverage and text filters on the other columns, header-click sorting and a 'Viewing rows x through y of z' counter. A summary sits above it (cutoff, node/edge counts, index size).
steps: Open the Annotations tab
Read the summary line
Type in column filters (e.g. Domain BP, Genes Q14119, Coverage min 4)
Click a header to sort
Clear filters
serves_tasks: Filter and sort the function table by column

features.name: Export of the filtered table and graph
features.general: Download the current filtered result as a spreadsheet file and the graph as a portable graph-description file.
features.specific: Download CSV file saves genescape.csv (Coverage, Function, Domain, GO, Genes) with the sidebar filters applied. Download DOT file saves genescape.dot.txt, a Graphviz digraph with the node labels and fill colours.
steps: Set filters and press Draw Tree
Click Download CSV file
Click Download DOT file
Open the files elsewhere (e.g. Graphviz, a spreadsheet)
